verdict_reason: Every finding from the ba740632 REJECTED delta is closed structurally, verified line by line against the real diff, not the commit message. HIGH fail-open (substring amnesty vs whole-token detection): dadaia_workspace/features/chokepoints/push_gate.py:79 ObjectSource.tree_mentions(term)->bool is DELETED; the port is tree_matches(patterns)->set[str] (push_gate.py:389 _published_slugs, push_gate.py:249 scan_slugs = [slug for slug in slug_list if slug not in published]). Both the detection side (denylist_scan.py:290 scan_objects -> compile_slug_patterns(scan_slugs)) and the amnesty side (push_gate.py:389 _published_slugs -> compile_slug_patterns(slugs)) compile patterns through the SAME function (denylist_scan.py:115 compile_slug_patterns, whole-token lookaround regex, re.escape(slug), re.IGNORECASE) -- amnesty is a subset of detection by construction, not by convention. The real adapter is exercised end-to-end by tests/integration/test_push_gate_denylist.py::test_published_slug_amnesty_is_never_broader_than_detection (added in 4e110f14): a slug glued into a longer identifier (zz-sibling-repo-x, ZZ-SIBLING-REPO.md, pkg.zz-sibling-repo) never amnesties; a bare case-different whole-token occurrence does -- pinned against GitSubprocessObjectReader.tree_matches, no fake in the loop. infrastructure/git_objects.py:929 tree_matches: argv injection -- subprocess.run(args, cwd=repo, ...) (git_objects.py _run, shell=False by default, no shell=True anywhere in this module), args is a list (['git','grep','-I','-i','-P','-o','-h'] + repeated ['-e', pattern] + [sha]) so no shell metacharacter interpretation is possible; sha is hex-gated by _SHA_SHAPE_RE (^[0-9a-fA-F]{40}$|^[0-9a-fA-F]{64}$) BEFORE it reaches argv (git_objects.py:939), rejecting an option-shaped value (e.g. --upload-pack=...) outright -- same guard pattern as the pre-existing _is_resolvable_commit (CWE-88 precedent). Each pattern is passed as its own argv element immediately after its own -e flag, never shell-joined, so a pattern beginning with '-' is still consumed as the -e operand, not reparsed as a flag. ReDoS: patterns are compile_slug_patterns output over slugs sourced from cli/commands/ci.py:310 _foreign_repo_slugs(workspace, own_slug, registry_result.identities) -- the workspace's own registry (associated_repos config), never attacker/push-controlled content -- and even so each pattern is `(?<![\w-])(?<!\w\.)` + re.escape(slug) + `(?![\w-])(?!\.\w)`: re.escape neutralizes every regex metacharacter in the slug, the lookarounds are fixed-width, and there is no nested/overlapping quantifier over a shared class -- linear-time, no catastrophic-backtracking shape, confirmed by reading all patterns denylist_scan.py:115-146. Fail-closed on read errors: git_objects.py:929 tree_matches raises GitObjectReadError on any exit code other than 0 or 1; push_gate.py's _RangeScan.read_failed discriminator (typed, not string-matched on refusal prose -- closes the MEDIUM) routes a read failure straight to a BLOCKED decision before the canon scan even runs (push_gate.py ~500: 'if scan.read_failed and scan.refusal is not None: return _annotate_skip(...)') -- amnesty on a read failure returns set() from _published_slugs's caller-side except GitObjectReadError, so nothing is amnestied, matching the docstring's 'amnesties nothing' claim. ci.py:285 pattern-version gate: `if specs_dir.is_dir() and specs_version < CANONICAL_SPECS_VERSION: canon_fn = _no_canon_violations` -- reading push_gate.py's push_gate_decision, canon_fn only ever feeds _run_specs_canon_scan; denylist_terms, baseline_patterns and foreign_slugs are threaded to _run_denylist_scan unconditionally and verdict_violations_fn (the verdict-rule check) is never touched by this branch -- the skip is scoped to the canon predicate alone, exactly as claimed, closing the MEDIUM. Secret/sibling-name redaction (CWE-200): `git grep -n -i -E 'dd-chain|chain-(capture|explorer)' HEAD -- specs/bugs/BUGS.jsonl specs/ADRs/decisions.jsonl dadaia_workspace/public/data/DADAIA.md` -> 0 matches (exit 1); re-run over the whole tracked tree at HEAD (excluding this verdicts directory) -> 0 matches (exit 1); d3fe9619 replaces the two evidence_loop fields' real sibling-repo paths with generic descriptors (repos/sample-consumer, repos/sample-consumer-infra); 448d365e replaces ADR 0013's context prose the same way -- both verified line-by-line against the diff, not the commit message. `git diff 62369eb9..HEAD | grep -nE '<home-dir>|[0-9]{1,3}(\.[0-9]{1,3}){3}'` produced exactly one hit (line 698 of the diff), entirely inside the superseded verdict's own quoted verdict_reason text describing a past grep pattern and an already-deleted file (matches the task's stated non-finding carve-out) -- not a new leak. Secret-pattern grep `(password|passwd|secret|token|api_key|apikey|private_key)\s*=\s*["'][^"']{6,}` and a BEGIN...PRIVATE KEY grep over the same delta diff: the only PRIVATE KEY hits are likewise inside the two old (now-superseded/deleted) verdict files' own prose describing pre-existing fixture hits in tests/unit/test_spec_context_service.py and infrastructure/privacy_check.py -- not live secrets, not new in this delta. DADAIA.md sec3.4/7.4 (public/data/DADAIA.md lines ~94-100, ~273-280): the new text ('pre-push scans the pushed range only: published history is the baseline and is never rescanned', 'the only amnesty is a term the baseline already publishes under the same matcher') does not weaken the secret/pattern scan -- confirmed against code: push_gate.py:249 filters ONLY scan_slugs (the foreign-repo-slug layer) by `published`; term_list (operator denylist terms) and pattern_list (baseline privacy/secret patterns) are passed to scan_objects unfiltered on every call, with no amnesty path reaching them anywhere in push_gate.py or denylist_scan.py. foreign_slugs itself is registry-sourced (ci.py:310), so only registered sibling-repo slugs are ever eligible for amnesty, never an arbitrary attacker-supplied term. Targeted test run: `pytest tests/unit/features/chokepoints tests/integration -k 'push or gate or chokepoint' -q -p no:cacheprovider` -> 159 passed, 300 deselected, 0 failed. pip-audit -l: 47 known vulnerabilities in dulwich 0.21.7, msgpack 1.1.2, pillow 12.2.0, pip 24.0, poetry 1.8.3 -- all pre-existing dev-venv packages; `git diff --stat 62369eb9..HEAD` touches no pyproject.toml/lockfile, confirming none of these are introduced or version-changed by this delta (out of scope per the task framing). One open governance-process note, not a security finding: d3fe9619's commit message states 'the write-once seam refused the redaction -- noted for intake', meaning specs/bugs/BUGS.jsonl was hand-edited (2 lines changed outside the normal `dadaia bugs update` governance verb) to perform the redaction because the ledger's write-once field discipline blocked doing it through the CLI; the redacted CONTENT is confirmed correct by the greps above, but the hand-edit itself is a DADAIA.md 8.5 LEDGER-BUGS-HANDEDIT-class event (WARNING-only, never a block) that the operator/PM should route to backlog intake so the governance-write seam gains a sanctioned redaction path. No CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM finding remains open. Nothing in this delta touches an authenticated production endpoint, a live credential, or introduces a dependency-version change. Snapshot, not a guarantee of 'secure' (DADAIA.md 7.5) -- the operator owns the ship decision.
